reject.camp: Mackinaw Shelter camp, North Fork Sauk
reject.reason: The route's only stated way in (White Chuck trail #643) was destroyed in 2003, as the reviewer's own flag says. The practical way to the Sitkum Creek/PCT junction and the Boulder Basin path today is NF Sauk -> White Pass -> PCT north over Red Pass. Mackinaw is the first night on that. Removing it leaves the route with only camps on a dead approach and the Suiattle side.

reject.camp: White Pass and the Foam Creek benches under White Mountain
reject.reason: White Pass is where the NF Sauk trail meets the PCT that runs north over Red Pass to the Sitkum Creek junction (where the Boulder Basin climbers' path starts). With #643 gone it is on the only short approach still in use.

reject.reason: The route's own second way in is 'the natural line for a party already high in this range on a multi-peak traverse', and its overview calls it 'one of the more scenic technical routes along the Ptarmigan Traverse'. Kool-Aid is that traverse's first camp. The route is treated the same as its neighbour Dome, which keeps these camps.
Same reason. This is the Ptarmigan Traverse's second camp, on the route's own traverse way in.
Route prose: Sinister 'sits on the classic Ptarmigan Traverse corridor'. Traverse parties reach it (as they reach Dome, which keeps these camps) through Kool-Aid.
Same reason: the traverse's second camp, on the corridor the route's own prose places the peak on.

Route overview: Spire Point stands 'along the classic Ptarmigan Traverse', and the route starts from Spire Col, which the traverse crosses. A north-to-south traverse party uses Kool-Aid as night one. This is the traverse-camp case. Note the inconsistency: for Old Guard the reviewer kept the southern traverse camps as 'traverse exit corridor'.
Same reason. Yang Yang is the standard second traverse night on the way to Spire Col, and the route's own overview places the peak on the Ptarmigan Traverse.
